procedures.name: Diagnose high CPU utilisation

steps.description: Open a remoting session to the server
Confirm sustained high CPU
Identify the top CPU-consuming processes
Review the top process. If it is a known runaway collector/agent (e.g. scheduled_task collector), reconfigure or restart it; if legitimate, confirm and document.
Verify CPU has returned to normal
Post work note: top process identified, action taken, CPU normalised

source_tickets: URGENT - iCapture Primary and DR servers high CPU utilization
ldn2ws0059 WARN -> CRIT CPU utilization
procedures.notes: Promoted from auto-draft. Real resolutions show: identify top CPU process then reconfigure/restart it (e.g. removed 'scheduled_task collector' from otel-config). Kept medium + a manual review step because the fix depends on which process is the culprit.

procedures.name: Linux disk capacity investigation (read-only)

steps.description: Open a read-only session to the Linux host
List filesystem usage to find the full mount
Identify the largest directories under the full mount
Confirm whether any mount is above the alert threshold
Decide what is safe to archive or remove (e.g. rotate/compress logs, clear old artefacts). Deletion is human-owned; BUCKY does not remove files.
Post work note: largest consumers identified; recommended cleanup for human action

procedures.name: Linux high CPU / memory / process investigation (read-only)

steps.description: Open a read-only session to the Linux host
Check load average and memory/swap pressure
Identify the top CPU and memory consumers
Confirm whether swap/memory pressure is sustained
Review the top process. If it is a known runaway, hand to the owning team to restart/reconfigure; BUCKY does not kill processes.
Post work note: resource pressure confirmed, top consumers identified
